key_insight: PDF-HR encodes humanoid robot poses as a continuous, differentiable Pose Distance Field, giving a lightweight, data-efficient prior that can be directly used in optimization and learning pipelines to improve pose and motion recovery.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of high-quality humanoid motion data and suitable priors by providing a compact, differentiable representation of valid humanoid poses that improves estimation, planning, and control under limited data.
method: Represent the distribution of humanoid poses as a continuous Pose Distance Field (PDF) that outputs distance-to-valid-pose and gradients for any query pose.
Learn/fit the PDF-HR from limited (real + synthetic) humanoid motion samples to capture the pose manifold compactly and differentiably.
Plug the PDF prior into downstream tasks (human-motion-recovery, state estimation, motion planning, controller optimization) to regularize solutions toward feasible humanoid poses.
impact: Provides a practical, easy-to-integrate prior that increases robustness and data-efficiency for humanoid pose estimation and motion planning; ML and robotics practitioners can use PDF-HR to impose kinematic/feasibility constraints with gradients.
visual_elements: 3D visualization of the Pose Distance Field around a humanoid skeleton (isosurfaces/heatmap showing distance to valid pose).
Pipeline diagram showing where PDF-HR plugs into perception → pose estimation → planner/controller loop.
Bar/line chart comparing accuracy and data-efficiency versus baseline priors across tasks (HMR, state estimation, planning).
Sequence of frames illustrating corrected/feasible motions before vs after applying PDF-HR.
paper_title: PDF-HR: Pose Distance Fields for Humanoid Robots
paper_authors: Yi Gu, Yukang Gao, Yangchen Zhou, Xingyu Chen, Yixiao Feng
